findings: src/execution/aggregate_hashtable.cpp:758 adds one condition, `layout_ptr->AllConstant()`, to the choice between staging new groups in `unpartitioned_data` and appending them straight to `partitioned_data`. The condition depends only on the physical layout type (whether it has heap columns such as VARCHAR or LIST). It names no query, table, column, literal or data size.

Correctness: the direct partitioned-append path was already used for any chunk with many new groups. Code downstream already handles an empty `unpartitioned_data` (Abandon, AcquirePartitionedData, Resize), so heap layouts take a path that already existed. This holds for NULLs, empty inputs, spilling and parallel execution.

There is no measurement tampering, no shift of cost to unmeasured phases, and no dead code. It is a minimal one-line change with an explanatory comment. The measured gain is small (about 5% median) but looks real, and it applies to any multi-threaded GROUP BY or DISTINCT on string keys.
